title: Choose the Thread-First composition
question: The visual world is locked. Which balance of agent thread, live browser, and review tools should Sylph build?

options.label: Persistent Preview
options.thesis: The thread owns the center while the live browser and change proof remain continuously visible at right.
options.viewport: Nested Repositories and Workspaces at left; agent thread and composer in the center; live browser above Changes and Checks at right.
options.risk: The browser remains persistent but is constrained when inspecting dense desktop layouts.

options.label: Wide Preview Crown
options.lineage: the same Thread-First world with a wide proof band
options.thesis: The live product spans the top of the work area while the agent narrative and review evidence continue together beneath it.
options.viewport: Nested left rail unchanged; a wide browser crown spans center and right; the thread runs below at center with Changes and Checks beside it.
options.risk: The horizontal browser band gives less uninterrupted vertical room to long conversations.

options.label: Tandem Workbench
options.lineage: the same Thread-First world with equal live surfaces
options.thesis: Agent and browser read as a paired workbench, with review evidence consolidated into a lower deck.
options.viewport: Nested left rail unchanged; agent and browser share the center in a stable 55/45 split; Files, Changes, Checks, and Skills form a lower deck.
options.risk: The paired surfaces are flexible but less opinionated about where attention should begin.
